objects.description: Abstract output interface for WOFF2 decoding. Supports appending and random-access writes as well as querying the current output size. Implementations enforce size limits (default suggested max is kDefaultMaxSize).
Concrete WOFF2Out that writes to and grows a std::string buffer up to a configurable maximum. Tracks a current write offset to support appends and random-access writes.
Concrete WOFF2Out that writes into a fixed-size memory buffer supplied by the caller. Supports bounded random-access writes; the size cannot grow beyond buf_size.
Parameter bundle for WOFF2 encoding. Holds optional extended metadata string to embed, Brotli compression quality (default 11), and whether table transform optimizations are allowed.

functions.name: woff2::WOFF2Out::Write
functions.signature: virtual bool woff2::WOFF2Out::Write(const void* buf, size_t n) = 0;
functions.description: Appends n bytes from buf to the end of the output stream used during WOFF2 decoding. Returns true if all bytes are written, false otherwise. Intended for producers that stream sequential output.
requirements: buf must point to at least n readable bytes when n > 0.
May fail (return false) if the implementation refuses to grow beyond its limit (by default often kDefaultMaxSize for implementations that enforce it).
Calling code should check the boolean return and stop or handle failure if false.
The current output size can be queried via Size().

functions.name: woff2::WOFF2Out::Write
functions.signature: virtual bool woff2::WOFF2Out::Write(const void* buf, size_t offset, size_t n) = 0;
functions.description: Writes n bytes from buf into the output at the specified offset. Supports random-access updates (e.g., to patch tables or checksums) during WOFF2 decoding. Returns true if all bytes are written, false otherwise.
requirements: buf must point to at least n readable bytes when n > 0.
offset must be within the implementation’s allowable range; writing may extend the output if supported by the implementation.
May fail (return false) if the write would exceed the implementation’s size limits (commonly capped by kDefaultMaxSize for growing buffers).
Calling code should check the boolean return and handle failure if false.

functions.name: woff2::WOFF2Out::Size
functions.signature: virtual size_t woff2::WOFF2Out::Size() = 0;
functions.description: Returns the current logical size of the output produced so far. Useful for building dependent tables (e.g., loca) while writing glyph data.
requirements: No arguments; can be called at any time defined by the concrete implementation.
Returned size is implementation-defined; callers should not assume it reflects allocated capacity—only the logical written size.

functions.name: woff2::WOFF2StringOut::WOFF2StringOut
functions.signature: explicit woff2::WOFF2StringOut::WOFF2StringOut(std::string* buf);
functions.description: Constructs an expanding, in-memory output that writes into the provided std::string. The string grows as data is written, up to a maximum size (default kDefaultMaxSize).
requirements: buf must be non-null and remain valid for the lifetime of the WOFF2StringOut instance.
buf may be pre-sized or empty before construction.
The buffer will grow to at most the current MaxSize().

functions.name: woff2::WOFF2StringOut::Write
functions.signature: bool woff2::WOFF2StringOut::Write(const void* buf, size_t n) override;
functions.description: Appends n bytes from buf to the underlying std::string, expanding it as needed up to MaxSize(). Returns true if the append completes; false if it would exceed MaxSize() or on failure.
requirements: buf must point to at least n readable bytes when n > 0.
The total size after appending must not exceed MaxSize(); otherwise the function returns false.
Caller must check the boolean return and handle failure.

functions.name: woff2::WOFF2StringOut::Write
functions.signature: bool woff2::WOFF2StringOut::Write(const void* buf, size_t offset, size_t n) override;
functions.description: Writes n bytes from buf at the specified offset within the underlying std::string, expanding the string as needed up to MaxSize(). Returns true if the write completes; false otherwise.
requirements: buf must point to at least n readable bytes when n > 0.
If offset + n exceeds the current size, the string may expand; the resulting size must not exceed MaxSize().
Caller must check the boolean return and handle failure.

functions.name: woff2::WOFF2StringOut::Size
functions.signature: size_t woff2::WOFF2StringOut::Size() override;
functions.description: Returns the current logical size (in bytes) of the data written to the underlying std::string.
requirements: No arguments; can be called at any time during output generation.

functions.name: woff2::WOFF2StringOut::MaxSize
functions.signature: size_t woff2::WOFF2StringOut::MaxSize();
functions.description: Returns the current maximum allowed size for the expanding string buffer. By default this is kDefaultMaxSize (128 MiB) unless changed via SetMaxSize().
requirements: No arguments. Returned value represents a limit that subsequent writes must respect.

functions.name: woff2::WOFF2StringOut::SetMaxSize
functions.signature: void woff2::WOFF2StringOut::SetMaxSize(size_t max_size);
functions.description: Sets the maximum allowed size for the expanding string buffer. Writes that would exceed this limit will fail.
requirements: max_size sets a hard limit on growth; callers should choose a value large enough to accommodate expected output.
Changing the limit after data has been written does not shrink existing data; it only affects future writes.

functions.name: woff2::WOFF2MemoryOut::WOFF2MemoryOut
functions.signature: woff2::WOFF2MemoryOut::WOFF2MemoryOut(uint8_t* buf, size_t buf_size);
functions.description: Constructs a fixed-size output that writes into a caller-provided memory buffer of size buf_size bytes. The output cannot grow beyond buf_size.
requirements: buf must be non-null and point to a writable buffer of at least buf_size bytes.
buf must remain valid for the lifetime of the WOFF2MemoryOut instance.
buf_size defines the maximum output size; writes that exceed it should fail.

functions.name: woff2::WOFF2MemoryOut::Write
functions.signature: bool woff2::WOFF2MemoryOut::Write(const void* buf, size_t n) override;
functions.description: Appends n bytes from buf to the fixed-size buffer, advancing the internal offset. Returns true on success; false if the write would exceed buf_size or on failure.
requirements: buf must point to at least n readable bytes when n > 0.
The append must not cause the written size to exceed buf_size; otherwise the function returns false.
Caller must check the boolean return and handle failure.

functions.name: woff2::WOFF2MemoryOut::Write
functions.signature: bool woff2::WOFF2MemoryOut::Write(const void* buf, size_t offset, size_t n) override;
functions.description: Writes n bytes from buf into the fixed-size buffer starting at offset. Returns true on success; false if offset + n exceeds buf_size or on failure.
requirements: buf must point to at least n readable bytes when n > 0.
offset + n must be <= buf_size; otherwise the function returns false.
Caller must check the boolean return and handle failure.

functions.name: woff2::WOFF2MemoryOut::Size
functions.signature: size_t woff2::WOFF2MemoryOut::Size() override;
functions.description: Returns the current logical number of bytes written to the fixed-size buffer.
requirements: No arguments; can be called at any time during output generation.

import random
import struct
from typing import List

# This generator produces interesting arbitrary binary strings to exercise:
# - WOFF2Out/WOFF2StringOut/WOFF2MemoryOut Write() with both append and offset forms
# - MaxWOFF2CompressedSize (expects TTF/OTF bytes) and ConvertTTFToWOFF2 encoders
# While the fuzzer accepts arbitrary bytes, providing realistic TTF/OTF-like inputs
# increases the chance of reaching deeper code paths. We generate a variety of
# valid or near-valid SFNT/TrueType-like byte sequences of small size.

# Limits
MAX_TOTAL = 4096

# Helpers to build big-endian fields

def be16(x: int) -> bytes:
    return struct.pack(">H", x & 0xFFFF)

def be32(x: int) -> bytes:
    return struct.pack(">I", x & 0xFFFFFFFF)

# Compute TrueType checksum as per spec (sum of big-endian 32-bit words, modulo 2^32)
# Pads table data to 4-byte boundary with zeroes.

def tt_checksum(data: bytes) -> int:
    n = len(data)
    pad = (4 - (n % 4)) % 4
    s = 0
    for i in range(0, n + pad, 4):
        chunk = data[i:i+4]
        if len(chunk) < 4:
            chunk = chunk + b"\x00" * (4 - len(chunk))
        s = (s + struct.unpack(">I", chunk)[0]) & 0xFFFFFFFF
    return s

# Build a minimal, consistent TrueType font with required tables: head, maxp, loca, glyf, hhea, hmtx, cmap.
# We construct one simple glyph (empty or a small contour), short or long loca depending on glyph data size.
# This is not a full-featured font but should be structurally valid enough for many parsers/encoders.

def build_minimal_ttf(seed: int, try_complex: bool) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Table builders return bytes; later we will compute offsets and checksums.
    # head: version 1.0, magic number 0x5F0F3CF5, unitsPerEm 2048, indexToLocFormat 0/1 set later
    def build_head(index_to_loc_format: int, checksum_adjustment: int = 0) -> bytes:
        version = be32(0x00010000)
        fontRevision = be32(0x00010000)
        checkSumAdjustment = be32(checksum_adjustment)
        magicNumber = be32(0x5F0F3CF5)
        flags = be16(0x000B)
        unitsPerEm = be16(2048)
        created = be32(0) + be32(0)
        modified = be32(0) + be32(0)
        xMin = be16(0)
        yMin = be16(0)
        xMax = be16(0)
        yMax = be16(0)
        macStyle = be16(0)
        lowestRecPPEM = be16(8)
        fontDirectionHint = be16(2)
        indexToLocFormat_be = be16(index_to_loc_format)
        glyphDataFormat = be16(0)
        return (
            version + fontRevision + checkSumAdjustment + magicNumber + flags + unitsPerEm +
            created + modified + xMin + yMin + xMax + yMax + macStyle + lowestRecPPEM +
            fontDirectionHint + indexToLocFormat_be + glyphDataFormat
        )

    # maxp: for TrueType version 1.0
    def build_maxp(numGlyphs: int) -> bytes:
        return (
            be32(0x00010000) + be16(numGlyphs) +
            be16(1) + be16(1) + be16(0) + be16(0) + be16(0) + be16(0) + be16(0) +
            be16(0) + be16(0) + be16(0) + be16(0) + be16(0) + be16(0) + be16(0)
        )

    # hhea: minimal metrics for 1 glyph
    def build_hhea() -> bytes:
        ascender = 800
        descender = -200 & 0xFFFF
        lineGap = 200
        advanceWidthMax = 512
        minLeftSideBearing = 0
        minRightSideBearing = 0
        xMaxExtent = 512
        caretSlopeRise = 1
        caretSlopeRun = 0
        reserved = b"\x00\x00" * 5
        metricDataFormat = be16(0)
        numberOfHMetrics = be16(1)
        return (
            be32(0x00010000) + be16(ascender) + be16(descender) + be16(lineGap) +
            be16(advanceWidthMax) + be16(minLeftSideBearing) + be16(minRightSideBearing) +
            be16(xMaxExtent) + be16(caretSlopeRise) + be16(caretSlopeRun) + reserved +
            metricDataFormat + numberOfHMetrics
        )

    # hmtx: one long metric for 1 glyph
    def build_hmtx() -> bytes:
        advanceWidth = 512
        lsb = 0
        return be16(advanceWidth) + be16(lsb)

    # cmap: format 4 or 0 (choose randomly). Provide mapping for glyph id 0 only.
    def build_cmap() -> bytes:
        if rng.random() < 0.5:
            # format 0 with 256 bytes
            glyphIdArray = bytes([0] * 256)
            subtable = be16(0) + be16(262) + be16(0) + glyphIdArray
            # cmap header: version, numTables=1, encoding (platform 3, encoding 1 for Unicode)
            header = be16(0) + be16(1) + be16(3) + be16(1) + be32(12)
            return header + subtable
        else:
            # format 4 minimal mapping for BMP range [0,0] -> glyph 0
            segCount = 1
            segCountX2 = be16(segCount * 2)
            searchRange = be16(2)
            entrySelector = be16(0)
            rangeShift = be16(0)
            endCount = be16(0)
            reservedPad = be16(0)
            startCount = be16(0)
            idDelta = be16(0)
            idRangeOffset = be16(0)
            # length: 14 + 2*segCount*4
            length = 14 + 8
            subtable = (
                be16(4) + be16(length) + be16(0) +
                segCountX2 + searchRange + entrySelector + rangeShift +
                endCount + reservedPad + startCount + idDelta + idRangeOffset
            )
            header = be16(0) + be16(1) + be16(3) + be16(1) + be32(12)
            return header + subtable

    # Simple glyph: either empty (no contours) or a tiny rectangle
    def build_glyf_and_loca(use_long_loca: bool):
        glyphs: List[bytes] = []
        if rng.random() < 0.5:
            # empty glyph (numContours = 0)
            g0 = be16(0) + be16(0) + be16(0) + be16(0) + be16(0)
        else:
            # one contour with 4 points (tiny box)
            numContours = 1
            xMin, yMin, xMax, yMax = 0, 0, 10, 10
            header = be16(numContours) + be16(xMin) + be16(yMin) + be16(xMax) + be16(yMax)
            endPtsOfContours = be16(3)
            instructionLength = be16(0)
            flags = bytes([
                0x01 | 0x02,  # on-curve, x-short
                0x01 | 0x12,  # on-curve, y-short, repeat
                0x01 | 0x00,  # on-curve
                0x01 | 0x10,  # on-curve, y-short
            ])
            # Coordinates as deltas per flags: keep tiny
            x = bytes([5, 0, 0, 0])
            y = bytes([0, 5, 0, 0])
            g0 = header + endPtsOfContours + instructionLength + flags + x + y
        # Align to 4 bytes
        pad = (4 - (len(g0) % 4)) % 4
        g0 += b"\x00" * pad
        glyphs.append(g0)

        glyf = b"".join(glyphs)
        # loca depends on indexToLocFormat
        if use_long_loca:
            offsets = [0, len(glyf)]
            loca = b"".join(be32(o) for o in offsets)
        else:
            # short loca uses offsets divided by 2
            offsets = [0, len(glyf) // 2]
            loca = b"".join(be16(o) for o in offsets)
        return glyf, loca

    # Decide loca format based on random and glyph size
    use_long = rng.random() < 0.5
    glyf0, loca0 = build_glyf_and_loca(use_long)

    # Build other tables
    maxp = build_maxp(1)
    hhea = build_hhea()
    hmtx = build_hmtx()
    cmap = build_cmap()

    # head requires checksum adjustment later; build with placeholder
    head = build_head(1 if use_long else 0, 0)

    # Assemble table directory
    tables = {
        b"head": head,
        b"maxp": maxp,
        b"hhea": hhea,
        b"hmtx": hmtx,
        b"cmap": cmap,
        b"loca": loca0,
        b"glyf": glyf0,
    }

    # Compute table records with 4-byte aligned offsets
    tags = sorted(tables.keys())
    numTables = len(tags)
    # sfnt header
    searchRange = 1
    entrySelector = 0
    while (1 << (entrySelector + 1)) <= numTables:
        entrySelector += 1
    searchRange = (1 << entrySelector) * 16
    rangeShift = numTables * 16 - searchRange

    directory = be32(0x00010000) + be16(numTables) + be16(searchRange) + be16(entrySelector) + be16(rangeShift)

    # Placeholder for table records
    records = []
    offset = 12 + numTables * 16
    # align helper
    def align4(x: int) -> int:
        return (x + 3) & ~3

    # Compute checksums and record entries; offsets filled after alignment pass
    # We'll first plan sizes and offsets
    planned = {}
    cur = offset
    for tag in tags:
        cur = align4(cur)
        planned[tag] = cur
        cur += align4(len(tables[tag]))

    # Build records
    for tag in tags:
        data = tables[tag]
        checksum = tt_checksum(data)
        rec = tag + be32(checksum) + be32(planned[tag]) + be32(len(data))
        records.append(rec)

    out = [directory] + records

    # Append table data at the exact planned offsets, adding padding as needed
    cursor = 12 + numTables * 16
    for tag in tags:
        # pad to 4-byte boundary
        pad_len = (4 - (cursor % 4)) % 4
        if pad_len:
            out.append(b"\x00" * pad_len)
            cursor += pad_len
        # verify planned offset
        assert cursor == planned[tag]
        data = tables[tag]
        out.append(data)
        cursor += len(data)
        # pad table to 4-byte boundary
        pad_len = (4 - (len(data) % 4)) % 4
        if pad_len:
            out.append(b"\x00" * pad_len)
            cursor += pad_len

    font = b"".join(out)

    # Fix head.checkSumAdjustment so that the whole font checksum becomes 0xB1B0AFBA
    # (as per TrueType spec)
    whole_sum = tt_checksum(font)
    adj = (0xB1B0AFBA - whole_sum) & 0xFFFFFFFF

    # Patch head table: checkSumAdjustment is at offset within head table (bytes 8..11)
    # Find head offset
    head_index = tags.index(b"head")
    # Directory starts at 12; record i starts at 12 + i*16
    head_rec_off = 12 + head_index * 16
    head_table_offset = struct.unpack(">I", font[head_rec_off + 8: head_rec_off + 12])[0]

    font = bytearray(font)
    font[head_table_offset + 8: head_table_offset + 12] = be32(adj)
    return bytes(font)

# Other interesting payload families for Write() sinks and metadata:

def random_ascii(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    letters = [
        ord('a'), ord('A'), ord('0'), ord('\n'), ord(' '), ord('\t'), ord('\x00')
    ]
    return bytes(rng.choice(letters) for _ in range(n))

def repeated_blocks(rng: random.Random, size: int) -> bytes:
    block_sizes = [1, 2, 3, 4, 8, 16, 64]
    block = bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(rng.choice(block_sizes)))
    reps = max(1, size // max(1, len(block)))
    data = (block * reps)[:size]
    return data

def small_woff2_magic(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Minimal WOFF2 header-like bytes to tick file-type sniffers: 'wOF2' + size fields
    sig = b"wOF2"
    # length, reserved, totalSfntSize, totalCompressedSize, major/minor, meta lengths etc.
    tail = be32(rng.randrange(16, 256)) + be32(0) + be32(rng.randrange(16, 512)) + be32(rng.randrange(16, 512)) + b"\x00\x01\x00\x00" + be32(0) + be32(0) + be32(0)
    return (sig + tail)[:min(64, MAX_TOTAL)]

# Top-level generator

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Choose a family of inputs with weighted probabilities.
    choice = rng.random()
    if choice < 0.50:
        # Build a small but structurally valid TTF (best for ConvertTTFToWOFF2/Max size)
        try_complex = rng.random() < 0.5
        data = build_minimal_ttf(seed ^ 0xA5A55A5A, try_complex)
    elif choice < 0.65:
        # WOFF2-like magic header to drive WOFF2 analysis paths (used as generic data in writes or metadata)
        data = small_woff2_magic(rng)
    elif choice < 0.80:
        # Repeated blocks for Write() sink exploration
        size = rng.randrange(0, min(2048, MAX_TOTAL))
        data = repeated_blocks(rng, size)
    else:
        # Random ASCII/control mix (useful for metadata and generic buffers)
        size = rng.randrange(0, min(2048, MAX_TOTAL))
        data = random_ascii(rng, size)

    # Ensure size cap and return bytes
    return bytes(data[:MAX_TOTAL])

import random
import struct

# Generator for compact WOFF2 byte streams. Produces many distinct variations
# while staying within spec-ish constraints expected by the stubs.

SIG_WOFF2 = 0x774F4632  # 'wOF2'
SIG_TTF = 0x00010000
SIG_OTTO = 0x4F54544F  # 'OTTO'


def _u16(x: int) -> bytes:
    return struct.pack(">H", x & 0xFFFF)


def _u32(x: int) -> bytes:
    return struct.pack(">I", x & 0xFFFFFFFF)


def _uvarint(n: int) -> bytes:
    # Unsigned base-128 big-endian varint (WOFF2)
    if n == 0:
        return b"\x00"
    chunks = []
    while n:
        chunks.append(n & 0x7F)
        n >>= 7
    out = bytearray()
    for i in range(len(chunks) - 1, -1, -1):
        b = chunks[i]
        if i != 0:
            b |= 0x80
        out.append(b)
    return bytes(out)


def _brotli_minimal_stream(kind: int) -> bytes:
    # Predefined tiny brotli streams (not payload-dependent). Different choices
    # give the fuzzer different compressed sizes and headers.
    # These are small streams accepted by decoders; we choose among a few.
    # We do not attempt full correctness of decompressed data, only container-level validity.
    variants = [
        b"\x06\x00",                      # empty stream
        b"\x0b\x00",                      # tiny stream variant
        b"\x1b\x00",                      # another tiny header-only
        b"\x03\x00",                      # short window
        b"\x0c\x00",                      # short block
    ]
    return variants[kind % len(variants)]


def _make_woff2_header(total_length: int, total_sfnt_size: int, num_tables: int, flavor: int,
                        total_compressed_size: int, meta_len=0, priv_len=0,
                        major=1, minor=0) -> bytearray:
    hdr = bytearray()
    hdr += _u32(SIG_WOFF2)             # signature
    hdr += _u32(flavor)                # flavor
    hdr += _u32(total_length)          # length (patched later)
    hdr += _u16(num_tables)            # numTables
    hdr += _u16(0)                     # reserved
    hdr += _u32(total_sfnt_size)       # totalSfntSize
    hdr += _u32(total_compressed_size) # totalCompressedSize
    hdr += _u16(major)                 # majorVersion
    hdr += _u16(minor)                 # minorVersion
    hdr += _u32(0)                     # metaOffset
    hdr += _u32(meta_len)              # metaLength
    hdr += _u32(0)                     # metaOrigLength
    hdr += _u32(0)                     # privOffset
    hdr += _u32(priv_len)              # privLength
    return hdr


def _dir_entry(tag: bytes, orig_len: int, transform=False, xform_len=None) -> bytes:
    # flags: [transform bit << 5] | tag_index (63 => explicit tag follows)
    flags = ((1 if transform else 0) << 5) | 63
    out = bytearray([flags])
    out += tag
    out += _uvarint(orig_len)
    if transform:
        out += _uvarint(0 if xform_len is None else xform_len)
    return bytes(out)


def _rand_tag(rnd: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Choose from common tags and random 4-char uppercase tags to diversify
    common = [b"head", b"name", b"OS/2", b"cmap", b"hhea", b"maxp", b"hmtx", b"post", b"loca", b"glyf", b"CFF "]
    if rnd.random() < 0.7:
        return rnd.choice(common)
    else:
        return bytes([rnd.randrange(65, 91) for _ in range(4)])


def _pick_flavor(rnd: random.Random) -> int:
    return SIG_TTF if rnd.random() < 0.8 else SIG_OTTO


def _build_font_variant(rnd: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Choose number of tables: mostly 0 or 1 to keep small, sometimes 2-3.
    num_tables = rnd.choices([0, 1, 2, 3], weights=[3, 4, 2, 1])[0]

    # Choose SFNT flavor
    flavor = _pick_flavor(rnd)

    # Build directory block
    directory = bytearray()
    directory += _uvarint(num_tables)

    # For SFNT sizing: header 12 + 16*num_tables + sum(padded table lengths)
    offset_first = 12 + 16 * num_tables
    table_lengths = []
    tags = []

    for _ in range(num_tables):
        tag = _rand_tag(rnd)
        # Choose plausible original length in [20, 256] and ensure DWORD padding calculation is stable
        orig_len = rnd.randrange(20, 257)
        transform = False
        directory += _dir_entry(tag, orig_len, transform)
        tags.append(tag)
        table_lengths.append(orig_len)

    padded_sum = sum((l + 3) & ~3 for l in table_lengths)
    total_sfnt = offset_first + padded_sum

    # Compressed tables block: choose among several tiny brotli streams; concatenate per table
    tables_block = bytearray()
    for i in range(max(1, num_tables)):  # ensure non-empty block for robustness
        tables_block += _brotli_minimal_stream(rnd.randrange(0, 5))
    total_compressed_size = len(tables_block)

    header = _make_woff2_header(0, total_sfnt, num_tables, flavor, total_compressed_size,
                                major=1, minor=0)
    body = bytearray()
    body += directory
    body += tables_block
    total_len = len(header) + len(body)
    header[8:12] = _u32(total_len)
    return bytes(header + body)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rnd = random.Random(seed)
    # Produce a mix of variants per call, seeded for repeatability while ensuring
    # across seeds we have high diversity.
    # We also add slight stochastic mixing inside a seed to avoid only-2 outputs.
    variants = []
    variants.append(_build_font_variant(rnd))
    # Occasionally build a second variant and pick one to diversify even within a seed
    if rnd.random() < 0.5:
        variants.append(_build_font_variant(rnd))
    return rnd.choice(variants)
